newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Ssangyong shares mixed on restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Ssangyong shares mixed on restructuring.

text.p: Shares of South Korea's Ssangyong Group were mixed in Wednesday morning trading after the group announced a business restructuring plan to cut its affiliates to 21 from the current 25, brokers said.
Ssangyong Motor Co lost 220 won to 5,520 and Ssangyong Precision Industry shed 180 won to 5,000.
But Ssangyong Cement added 200 won to 9,650 and Ssangyong Oil Refining remained unchanged at 17,900.

A Ssangyong group statement said Ssangyong Heavy Industries Co Ltd would absorb Ssangyong Precision, and unlisted Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Co would merge with Ssangyong Engineering Co Ltd.
"We aim to maximise management efficiency through the restructuring," a group spokesman said.

Analysts said financial problems in the nation's sixth largest conglomerate had surfaced when its automaking unit, Ssangyong Motor, said it would sell its headquarters and other assets to raise about 400 billion won.
They said the trouble had been reflected in the group shares, with seven of the 10 listed Ssangyong Group shares trading at below 10,000 won.
An LG Securities analyst said the goal of the restructuring plan was to salvage the cash-strapped Ssangyong Motor. "But the annoucement is not enough to help finance the automaker."
"Investors took a wait-and-see attitude as they are not sure whether the business restructuring news is positive or negative for the group in general," said a Sungkyong Securities broker.
But a broker at a local securities house said he was pessimistic over Ssangyong's plan as the group could not gain much by merging unprofitable business lines.
